# 1. Project overview

This analysis tests whether the **cluster membership produced by the
unsupervised clustering stage adds predictive value** for CRC risk.

Two models are compared:

1. Logistic Regression — without cluster membership
2. Logistic Regression — with cluster membership
3. Random Forest — without cluster membership
4. Random Forest — with cluster membership

A **70/30 stratified train/test split** is created once. The test set is kept
untouched until final evaluation. Model selection is performed using repeated
5-fold cross-validation on the training data.

A further methodological improvement is that the clustering model used to
create the cluster feature is fitted on the **training set only** and then
applied to the held-out test set. This avoids allowing the test observations to
influence the cluster feature.

# 2. Load packages

```{r libraries}
required_packages <- c(
  "caret",
  "mclust",
  "randomForest",
  "pROC",
  "ggplot2",
  "dplyr"
)

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Missing package(s): ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "),
      ". Install them once with:\ninstall.packages(c(",
      paste0('"', missing_packages, '"', collapse = ", "),
      "))"
    )
  )
}

library(caret)
library(mclust)
library(randomForest)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```

# 3. Load the clustered dataset

```{r load-data}
data_file <- "crc_data_with_clusters.csv"

if (!file.exists(data_file)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Cannot find '", data_file, "'. ",
      "Run the clustering Rmd first and keep the resulting CSV ",
      "in the same folder as this Rmd."
    )
  )
}

df <- read.csv(data_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

cat("Rows:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Columns:", ncol(df), "\n")
head(df)
```

# 4. Prepare the target and predictors

## 4.1 Check the required columns

```{r check-columns}
required_columns <- c(
  "Age", "Gender", "BMI", "Lifestyle", "Ethnicity",
  "Family_History_CRC", "Pre-existing Conditions",
  "Carbohydrates (g)", "Proteins (g)", "Fats (g)",
  "Vitamin A (IU)", "Vitamin C (mg)", "Iron (mg)", "CRC_Risk"
)

missing_required <- setdiff(required_columns, names(df))

if (length(missing_required) > 0) {
  stop(
    paste("Missing required columns:",
          paste(missing_required, collapse = ", "))
  )
}

cat("All required columns are present.\n")
```

## 4.2 Clean variable types

```{r clean-types}
numeric_predictors <- c(
  "Age", "BMI",
  "Carbohydrates (g)", "Proteins (g)", "Fats (g)",
  "Vitamin A (IU)", "Vitamin C (mg)", "Iron (mg)"
)

for (v in numeric_predictors) {
  df[[v]] <- as.numeric(df[[v]])
}

df$CRC_Risk <- factor(
  df$CRC_Risk,
  levels = c(0, 1),
  labels = c("No", "Yes")
)

if (anyNA(df$CRC_Risk)) {
  stop("CRC_Risk contains missing or unexpected values after conversion.")
}

cat("Outcome counts:\n")
print(table(df$CRC_Risk))
```

# 5. Train/test split

The same observations are used in every model comparison.

```{r split}
set.seed(42)

train_idx <- createDataPartition(
  df$CRC_Risk,
  p = 0.70,
  list = FALSE
)

train_raw <- df[train_idx, , drop = FALSE]
test_raw  <- df[-train_idx, , drop = FALSE]

cat("Training observations:", nrow(train_raw), "\n")
cat("Test observations:", nrow(test_raw), "\n")
```

# 6. Build a leakage-safe cluster feature

The original clustering output is useful for integration, but for a rigorous
predictive evaluation the cluster solution should not be learned using the
test observations.

Here, Mclust is fitted using **training observations only** and the resulting
cluster model is used to classify the test observations.

```{r train-cluster-model}
cluster_features <- c(
  "BMI",
  "Carbohydrates (g)",
  "Proteins (g)",
  "Fats (g)",
  "Vitamin A (IU)",
  "Vitamin C (mg)",
  "Iron (mg)"
)

for (v in cluster_features) {
  if (anyNA(train_raw[[v]])) {
    train_raw[[v]][is.na(train_raw[[v]])] <-
      median(train_raw[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  if (anyNA(test_raw[[v]])) {
    # Use training-set medians for test data: no test-set information
    # is used to estimate preprocessing values.
    test_raw[[v]][is.na(test_raw[[v]])] <-
      median(train_raw[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

cluster_train_scaled <- scale(
  train_raw[, cluster_features, drop = FALSE]
)

cluster_center <- attr(cluster_train_scaled, "scaled:center")
cluster_scale  <- attr(cluster_train_scaled, "scaled:scale")

cluster_test_scaled <- scale(
  test_raw[, cluster_features, drop = FALSE],
  center = cluster_center,
  scale = cluster_scale
)

# Mclust internally evaluates mclustBIC(), so the mclust package
# is attached explicitly before fitting the model.
if (!exists("mclustBIC", mode = "function")) {
  stop(
    "The mclust package is installed but mclustBIC() is unavailable. ",
    "Please restart R and run: install.packages("mclust")"
  )
}

set.seed(42)

cluster_model <- Mclust(
  cluster_train_scaled,
  G = 2:8
)

train_cluster <- cluster_model$classification

test_cluster_prediction <- predict(
  cluster_model,
  newdata = cluster_test_scaled
)

test_cluster <- test_cluster_prediction$classification

cat("Training-set BIC-selected G:", cluster_model$G, "\n")
cat("Covariance model:", cluster_model$modelName, "\n")
```

# 7. Prepare model matrices

The categorical predictors are converted to indicator variables using
`model.matrix()`. This avoids dependence on `fastDummies` and makes the
workflow easier to reproduce.

```{r model-matrices}
predictor_names <- c(
  "Age", "Gender", "BMI", "Lifestyle", "Ethnicity",
  "Family_History_CRC", "Pre-existing Conditions",
  "Carbohydrates (g)", "Proteins (g)", "Fats (g)",
  "Vitamin A (IU)", "Vitamin C (mg)", "Iron (mg)"
)

train_predictors <- train_raw[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE]
test_predictors  <- test_raw[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE]

# Impute categorical variables using training-set mode.
categorical_predictors <- c(
  "Gender", "Lifestyle", "Ethnicity",
  "Family_History_CRC", "Pre-existing Conditions"
)

mode_value <- function(x) {
  tab <- table(x, useNA = "no")
  names(tab)[which.max(tab)]
}

for (v in categorical_predictors) {
  if (anyNA(train_predictors[[v]])) {
    train_predictors[[v]][is.na(train_predictors[[v]])] <- mode_value(train_predictors[[v]])
  }

  if (anyNA(test_predictors[[v]])) {
    test_predictors[[v]][is.na(test_predictors[[v]])] <- mode_value(train_predictors[[v]])
  }

  train_predictors[[v]] <- factor(train_predictors[[v]])
  test_predictors[[v]] <- factor(
    test_predictors[[v]],
    levels = levels(train_predictors[[v]])
  )

  # Any genuinely new test category becomes NA; replace it with the training mode.
  if (anyNA(test_predictors[[v]])) {
    test_predictors[[v]][is.na(test_predictors[[v]])] <-
      levels(train_predictors[[v]])[1]
  }
}

# Numeric imputation uses training-set medians.
for (v in numeric_predictors) {
  if (anyNA(train_predictors[[v]])) {
    train_predictors[[v]][is.na(train_predictors[[v]])] <-
      median(train_predictors[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  if (anyNA(test_predictors[[v]])) {
    test_predictors[[v]][is.na(test_predictors[[v]])] <-
      median(train_predictors[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
  }
}

# Create matching dummy-variable columns.
x_train_base <- model.matrix(
  ~ . - 1,
  data = train_predictors
)

x_test_base <- model.matrix(
  ~ . - 1,
  data = test_predictors
)

# Align test columns exactly with training columns.
missing_test_columns <- setdiff(colnames(x_train_base), colnames(x_test_base))

if (length(missing_test_columns) > 0) {
  for (v in missing_test_columns) {
    x_test_base <- cbind(x_test_base, setNames(data.frame(rep(0, nrow(x_test_base))), v))
  }
}

extra_test_columns <- setdiff(colnames(x_test_base), colnames(x_train_base))

if (length(extra_test_columns) > 0) {
  x_test_base <- x_test_base[, setdiff(colnames(x_test_base), extra_test_columns), drop = FALSE]
}

x_test_base <- x_test_base[, colnames(x_train_base), drop = FALSE]

y_train <- train_raw$CRC_Risk
y_test  <- test_raw$CRC_Risk
```

# 8. Add cluster membership

The cluster feature is appended to a copy of the model matrix.

```{r add-cluster}
x_train_with_cluster <- cbind(
  x_train_base,
  Cluster = factor(train_cluster)
)

x_test_with_cluster <- cbind(
  x_test_base,
  Cluster = factor(
    test_cluster,
    levels = levels(factor(train_cluster))
  )
)

# model.matrix is used again so Cluster is represented consistently.
cluster_train_dummy <- model.matrix(~ Cluster - 1, data = data.frame(Cluster = factor(train_cluster)))
cluster_test_dummy  <- model.matrix(
  ~ Cluster - 1,
  data = data.frame(
    Cluster = factor(
      test_cluster,
      levels = levels(factor(train_cluster))
    )
  )
)

x_train_with_cluster <- cbind(
  x_train_base,
  cluster_train_dummy
)

x_test_with_cluster <- cbind(
  x_test_base,
  cluster_test_dummy
)

colnames(x_train_with_cluster) <- make.names(colnames(x_train_with_cluster))
colnames(x_test_with_cluster)  <- make.names(colnames(x_test_with_cluster))
```

# 9. Repeated cross-validation

All model tuning occurs inside the training set.

```{r cv-control}
cv_control <- trainControl(
  method = "repeatedcv",
  number = 5,
  repeats = 3,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  verboseIter = FALSE
)
```

# 10. Train four models

## 10.1 Logistic regression — without cluster

```{r logit-no-cluster}
set.seed(42)

logit_no_cluster <- train(
  x = x_train_base,
  y = y_train,
  method = "glm",
  family = binomial(),
  trControl = cv_control,
  metric = "ROC"
)
```

## 10.2 Logistic regression — with cluster

```{r logit-with-cluster}
set.seed(42)

logit_with_cluster <- train(
  x = x_train_with_cluster,
  y = y_train,
  method = "glm",
  family = binomial(),
  trControl = cv_control,
  metric = "ROC"
)
```

## 10.3 Random Forest — without cluster

```{r rf-no-cluster}
set.seed(42)

rf_no_cluster <- train(
  x = x_train_base,
  y = y_train,
  method = "rf",
  trControl = cv_control,
  metric = "ROC",
  tuneLength = 3,
  importance = TRUE
)
```

## 10.4 Random Forest — with cluster

```{r rf-with-cluster}
set.seed(42)

rf_with_cluster <- train(
  x = x_train_with_cluster,
  y = y_train,
  method = "rf",
  trControl = cv_control,
  metric = "ROC",
  tuneLength = 3,
  importance = TRUE
)
```

# 11. Cross-validated performance

```{r cv-results}
cv_results <- resamples(
  list(
    "Logistic — without cluster" = logit_no_cluster,
    "Logistic — with cluster" = logit_with_cluster,
    "Random Forest — without cluster" = rf_no_cluster,
    "Random Forest — with cluster" = rf_with_cluster
  )
)

print(summary(cv_results))
```

```{r cv-boxplot}
bwplot(
  cv_results,
  metric = "ROC",
  main = "Repeated 5-fold cross-validated ROC-AUC"
)
```

# 12. Final hold-out evaluation

The test set has not been used for model selection.

```{r holdout-predictions}
prob_logit_no <- predict(
  logit_no_cluster,
  newdata = x_test_base,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Yes"]

prob_logit_with <- predict(
  logit_with_cluster,
  newdata = x_test_with_cluster,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Yes"]

prob_rf_no <- predict(
  rf_no_cluster,
  newdata = x_test_base,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Yes"]

prob_rf_with <- predict(
  rf_with_cluster,
  newdata = x_test_with_cluster,
  type = "prob"
)[, "Yes"]

roc_logit_no <- roc(y_test, prob_logit_no, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
roc_logit_with <- roc(y_test, prob_logit_with, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
roc_rf_no <- roc(y_test, prob_rf_no, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
roc_rf_with <- roc(y_test, prob_rf_with, levels = c("No", "Yes"), direction = "<", quiet = TRUE)
```

# 13. Model comparison table

```{r comparison-table}
results <- data.frame(
  Model = c(
    "Logistic Regression",
    "Logistic Regression",
    "Random Forest",
    "Random Forest"
  ),
  Cluster_Feature = c(
    "Without",
    "With",
    "Without",
    "With"
  ),
  CV_ROC_Mean = c(
    mean(logit_no_cluster$resample$ROC),
    mean(logit_with_cluster$resample$ROC),
    mean(rf_no_cluster$resample$ROC),
    mean(rf_with_cluster$resample$ROC)
  ),
  Holdout_AUC_ROC = c(
    as.numeric(auc(roc_logit_no)),
    as.numeric(auc(roc_logit_with)),
    as.numeric(auc(roc_rf_no)),
    as.numeric(auc(roc_rf_with))
  )
)

results$AUC_Change_vs_No_Cluster <- c(
  NA,
  results$Holdout_AUC_ROC[2] - results$Holdout_AUC_ROC[1],
  NA,
  results$Holdout_AUC_ROC[4] - results$Holdout_AUC_ROC[3]
)

results$Meets_0.75_Target <- results$Holdout_AUC_ROC >= 0.75

print(results)
```

# 14. ROC curves

```{r roc-curves}
plot(
  roc_logit_no,
  main = "Hold-out ROC curves",
  lwd = 2
)

lines(roc_logit_with, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
lines(roc_rf_no, lwd = 2)
lines(roc_rf_with, lwd = 2, lty = 2)

legend(
  "bottomright",
  legend = c(
    "Logistic — without cluster",
    "Logistic — with cluster",
    "Random Forest — without cluster",
    "Random Forest — with cluster"
  ),
  lty = c(1, 2, 1, 2),
  lwd = 2,
  cex = 0.75
)

abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 3)
```

# 15. Does clustering improve prediction?

```{r cluster-value}
logit_change <- results$AUC_Change_vs_No_Cluster[2]
rf_change <- results$AUC_Change_vs_No_Cluster[4]

cat("Logistic Regression AUC change from adding cluster:",
    round(logit_change, 4), "\n")

cat("Random Forest AUC change from adding cluster:",
    round(rf_change, 4), "\n")

if (logit_change > 0) {
  cat("Cluster membership improves hold-out AUC for Logistic Regression.\n")
} else if (logit_change < 0) {
  cat("Cluster membership reduces hold-out AUC for Logistic Regression.\n")
} else {
  cat("Cluster membership produces no change in hold-out AUC for Logistic Regression.\n")
}

if (rf_change > 0) {
  cat("Cluster membership improves hold-out AUC for Random Forest.\n")
} else if (rf_change < 0) {
  cat("Cluster membership reduces hold-out AUC for Random Forest.\n")
} else {
  cat("Cluster membership produces no change in hold-out AUC for Random Forest.\n")
}
```

# 16. Confusion matrix for the best model

The best model is selected automatically using the **hold-out AUC**, then its
classification performance is displayed.

```{r best-model}
best_row <- which.max(results$Holdout_AUC_ROC)

best_name <- paste(
  results$Model[best_row],
  results$Cluster_Feature[best_row]
)

cat("Best model:", best_name, "\n")
cat("Hold-out AUC:", round(results$Holdout_AUC_ROC[best_row], 4), "\n")

best_model <- list(
  logit_no = logit_no_cluster,
  logit_with = logit_with_cluster,
  rf_no = rf_no_cluster,
  rf_with = rf_with_cluster
)[[
  c(
    "logit_no",
    "logit_with",
    "rf_no",
    "rf_with"
  )[best_row]
]]

best_newdata <- list(
  logit_no = x_test_base,
  logit_with = x_test_with_cluster,
  rf_no = x_test_base,
  rf_with = x_test_with_cluster
)[[
  c(
    "logit_no",
    "logit_with",
    "rf_no",
    "rf_with"
  )[best_row]
]]

best_class <- predict(best_model, newdata = best_newdata)

cm <- confusionMatrix(
  best_class,
  y_test,
  positive = "Yes"
)

print(cm)
```

```{r confusion-plot}
cm_df <- as.data.frame(cm$table)

ggplot(
  cm_df,
  aes(x = Reference, y = Prediction, fill = Freq)
) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 6) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Confusion matrix —", best_name),
    x = "Actual class",
    y = "Predicted class",
    fill = "Count"
  )
```

# 17. Random Forest variable importance

The Random Forest with cluster membership is inspected for interpretability.

```{r importance}
plot(
  varImp(rf_with_cluster),
  top = 15,
  main = "Top Random Forest predictors — with cluster membership"
)
```

# 18. Final report summary

```{r final-summary}
best_auc <- results$Holdout_AUC_ROC[best_row]

cat("========================================\n")
cat("CLASSIFICATION SUMMARY\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Training observations: ", nrow(train_raw), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Test observations: ", nrow(test_raw), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Cluster model G: ", cluster_model$G, "\n", sep = "")
cat("Best model: ", best_name, "\n", sep = "")
cat("Best hold-out AUC-ROC: ", round(best_auc, 4), "\n", sep = "")
cat("Meets AUC >= 0.75 target: ",
    ifelse(best_auc >= 0.75, "YES", "NO"), "\n", sep = "")
cat("========================================\n")
```

```{r save-results}
write.csv(

)

cat("Saved classification results to classification_results.csv\n")
```
